newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mixed, marks and Swiss lower.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mixed, marks and Swiss lower.

text.p: IMM currency futures finished mixed, with March marks and Swiss francs lower.
March yen finished higher, but near the bottom of the day's range after offers came in from $0.008900 to $0.008890, a floor manager for an IMM trading desk said.
Another trader said those sales totalled about 860 contracts in the last 20 minutes of trade.
Overall, they said trading was light as the focus remained on the Federal Reserve's inactivity and on volatility in U.S. stocks.
"It was relatively quiet," the floor manager said.
"We did see a flurry of activity in the yen, but for the most part it was range trading," he said.
Earlier gains in most contracts were wiped out when U.S. stocks staged an afternoon rebound, underpinning the dollar and capping currency strength, traders said.
One IMM currency futures trader said short-covering in dollar/mark as the European session came to a close also helped return March marks to negative territory.
Earlier currency gains had been tied to stronger-than-expected November housing starts.
Starts rose 9.2 percent to a 1.51 million annual rate, much higher than the forecast and a reversal from a 5.1-percent drop in October.

The strong housing starts number--released just after currencies opened--weighed on U.S. Treasury bonds early and caused stocks to open weaker, pulling the dollar from overnight gains against the mark and yen.
The mark was weak overnight on news the Bank of France cut its intervention rate by five basis points.
The yen was capped by comments from a Japanese official calling for a weaker yen.
One IMM currency futures trader noted heavy activity in March peso futures. He said funds were early buyers, with wire houses piling on later.
March sterling was strong as players looked favorably upon cable as the safe-haven for EMU concerns.
"Fundamentally that market looks really good, but volume was very very light," an IMM trader said.

March yen closed up $0.000011 to $0.008894, marks ended down $0.0011 to $0.6489, Swiss francs lost $0.0015 to $0.7610, Sterling jumped $0.0052 to $1.6672, Canadian dollar rose $0.0017 to $0.7372, Australian dollar added $0.0016 to $0.7948, and Mexican peso rallied $0.000850 to $0.121100.
